_doc: Files intentionally left git-ignored inside scheduled-tasks/<id>/ (CC/MCP fleet only -- the only tree covered by the ora-claude-config git backup) -- reviewed and judged to be genuine runtime state, not a durability gap. Consumed by task-folder-backup-completeness-probe.py. Adding an entry here is a per-file judgment call, same bar as ora-appsec-sweep/suppressions.md: only Gabriel adds entries. A finding NOT on this list means either allow-list it in .gitignore (durable fix -- the probe then stops flagging it automatically, since git check-ignore will report it as no-longer-ignored) or add it here with a dated reason.

exempt.reason: Per-run decision-history state the task writes to itself. Loss re-surfaces already-decided sessions (annoying, recoverable via re-decision) rather than losing ratified content (suppressions.md class) or an engine (guard.ps1 class) -- correctly excluded under the existing 2b rationale ('runtime state ... stays ignored').

Rewritten on effectively every scheduled poll (content-hash + commit-SHA gate, per-run golden-set dispersion samples, provenance notes). Same class as doctrine-status.json/fleet-roster.md/phantom-dispatch.json -- regenerated by a local script only, no external/CI reader, tracking it would churn a commit on every eval-harness fire for no reader. Point-in-time notes (e.g. a rebaselining recommendation) are lost if the file is ever corrupted with nothing else durably recording them -- accepted trade-off, not a gap to fix separately.
